To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ultrasound evaluation of the thyroid gland after radiation therapy and chemotherapy to treat malignancy during childhood is safe, feasible, and provides useful information for the management of these patients.
ultrasound is an effective method to detect and characterize thyroid nodules and masses after radiation therapy and chemotherapy to treat malignancy during childhood.

the ultrasound (US) findings of the thyroid gland in childhood cancer survivors (CCSs) after radiation therapy (RT) and/or chemotherapy (CT) for malignancy during childhood were as follows: US findings of the thyroid were abnormal in 60% of the CCSs, including 25% with thyroiditis and 35% with nodules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effects of ionizing radiation on the thyroid gland in patients who have received radiation therapy to the neck for the treatment of malignancy during childhood.
the evaluation of thyroid gland pathologies after chemotherapy and/or radiation therapy for malignancies during childhood.
the development of a new method for the evaluation of thyroid function after radiation therapy and chemotherapy in children and adolescents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no significant difference between ultrasound and scintigraphy for the detection of recurrent or residual thyroid cancer after treatment.
there is no evidence to suggest a causal relationship between radiation exposure during childhood and the development of thyroid nodules and thyroid cancers in adulthood.
there is no evidence of an association between childhood cancer and subsequent thyroid dysfunction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this research provides the initial evidence for the association between radiation therapy and thyroid cancer.

the use of ultrasound in the evaluation of thyroid gland pathologies after radiation therapy (RT) and chemotherapy (CT) to treat malignancy during childhood is a safe and effective modality that can provide accurate information for the diagnosis and treatment of these pathologies.

the use of a novel, noninvasive imaging technique, ultrasound elastography, can detect and characterize thyroid gland pathologies in survivors of childhood cancer who have undergone radiation therapy or chemotherapy to treat malignancy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no difference in the incidence of radiation thyroiditis in children and adults.
the majority of thyroid nodules in patients who received radiation for malignancy during childhood are benign.
the thyroid gland can be affected in the long term after radiation therapy and chemotherapy in childhood.
